subject: maths

concepts.title: Definition of a Set
concepts.definition: A collection of distinct objects where it is possible to determine with certainty whether any specific item is a member or not.
question_patterns: is the following collection a set
determine if the collection is well-defined
justify why the collection is or is not a set
identify sets from the given list
Explain the method of Definition of a Set.

solution_steps.explain: Evaluate if the criteria for inclusion is objective or subjective.
If the criteria is objective and consistent for everyone, it is a set.
Test boundary cases to confirm the membership decision is unambiguous for every candidate object.

concepts.title: Roster or Tabular Form
concepts.definition: A method of representing a set by explicitly listing every element inside curly brackets, separated by commas.
concepts.key_idea: Order of elements does not matter and repetitions are ignored.
question_patterns: write the set in roster form
represent the following in tabular form
convert the description to roster notation
list the elements of the set
Explain the method of Roster or Tabular Form.

solution_steps.explain: Find all individual items that satisfy the given condition.
Place the identified items inside { } separated by commas, removing duplicates.
Confirm that order of elements does not matter and no element is repeated in the final listing.

concepts.title: Set-Builder Form
concepts.definition: A notation that describes a set by stating the shared property that all its members must uniquely satisfy.
concepts.key_idea: Uses a variable and a characteristic property.
question_patterns: write the set in set-builder form
describe the set using a characteristic property
convert roster form to set-builder notation
express the set using a rule
Explain the method of Set-Builder Form.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the rule or mathematical condition shared by all elements.
Use the format {x : x satisfies property} to describe the set.
Ensure every element satisfying the property is included and no outside element accidentally meets the condition.

concepts.title: The Empty Set
concepts.definition: A set that contains no elements at all, also referred to as a null or void set.
concepts.key_idea: Zero cardinality; it is a subset of every set.
question_patterns: is the given set empty
identify the null set
give an example of a void set
check if the set has any elements
Explain the method of The Empty Set.

solution_steps.explain: Check if any object exists that satisfies the set's definition.
If no such object exists, the set is empty.
Cross-check by attempting to list at least one member; failure to do so confirms the set is the empty set.

concepts.title: Finite and Infinite Sets
concepts.definition: A set is finite if it is empty or has a countable number of elements; otherwise, it is infinite.
concepts.formula: n(A) = k (where k is a whole number)
concepts.key_idea: Finite sets have a terminable counting process.
question_patterns: state whether the set is finite or infinite
is the collection of ... a finite set
determine the nature of the set
classify the set based on element count
Explain the method of Finite and Infinite Sets.

solution_steps.explain: Attempt to list or count the distinct members of the set.
If counting ends, it is finite; if it continues indefinitely, it is infinite.
Provide reasoning by referencing the nature of the elements, such as whether they form a bounded or unbounded collection.

concepts.title: Equal Sets
concepts.definition: Two sets are considered equal if they possess exactly the same elements, regardless of the order of listing.
concepts.formula: A = B iff (x in A <=> x in B)
question_patterns: are the sets A and B equal
find pairs of equal sets
check for set equality
verify if A = B
Explain the method of Equal Sets.

solution_steps.explain: Check if every element of the first set is in the second and vice versa.
If all elements match exactly, the sets are equal.
Confirm both sets have the same number of elements, since equal sets must have identical cardinality.

concepts.title: Subsets
concepts.definition: A set A is a subset of B if every single element found in A is also present in B.
concepts.formula: A subset B <=> (x in A => x in B)
question_patterns: is A a subset of B
write all subsets of the set
find the number of subsets
check the inclusion relation
Explain the method of Subsets.

solution_steps.explain: Verify if each member of the smaller set exists in the larger set.
If all members are present in the second set, the first is a subset.
Conclude whether A is a subset of B, and note that every set is a subset of itself and the empty set is a subset of every set.

concepts.title: Intervals as Subsets of R
concepts.definition: Continuous segments of the real number line defined by their endpoints, which may be included or excluded.
concepts.key_idea: Open and closed brackets denote exclusion or inclusion of boundaries.
question_patterns: write the interval in set-builder form
represent the set as an interval
find the length of the interval
convert (a, b] to a set description
Explain the method of Intervals as Subsets of R.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the lower bound a and upper bound b.
The length is the difference between the upper and lower limits.
Use open or closed brackets to indicate whether endpoints are excluded or included in the interval.

concepts.title: Union of Sets
concepts.definition: A set containing all elements that belong to at least one of the given sets.
concepts.formula: A union B = {x : x in A or x in B}
question_patterns: find the union of sets A and B
calculate A union B
what is the union of the following
combine the sets
Explain the method of Union of Sets.

solution_steps.explain: Gather every element from all sets involved.
List each unique element exactly once in the final set.
Confirm that every element from each original set appears in the union and no element has been omitted.

concepts.title: Intersection of Sets
concepts.definition: A set consisting only of elements that are common to all the sets being considered.
concepts.formula: A intersection B = {x : x in A and x in B}
question_patterns: find the intersection of sets
what are the common elements
calculate A intersection B
determine if sets are disjoint
Explain the method of Intersection of Sets.

solution_steps.explain: Look for elements that appear in every set listed.
List these common elements within braces.
If no common elements exist, the intersection is the empty set, meaning the sets are disjoint.

concepts.title: Difference of Sets
concepts.definition: The set of elements that belong to the first set but are not present in the second set.
concepts.formula: A - B = {x : x in A and x not in B}
concepts.key_idea: Subtraction of common elements from the first set.
question_patterns: find A - B
calculate the difference of sets
what elements are in A but not in B
find B - A
Explain the method of Difference of Sets.

solution_steps.explain: Take all elements of set A.
Discard any elements that also appear in set B.
List the remaining elements of A within braces to form the result A - B.

concepts.title: Complement of a Set
concepts.definition: The set of all elements in the universal set that do not belong to the given set.
concepts.key_idea: Everything in the universe except the set itself.
question_patterns: find the complement of set A
calculate A'
what is the complement relative to U
find (A union B)'
Explain the method of Complement of a Set.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the full domain U.
List all members of U that are not in the specified set.
Confirm that the union of the set and its complement equals the universal set U, and their intersection is empty.

concepts.title: De Morgan's Laws
concepts.definition: Mathematical rules stating that the complement of a union is the intersection of complements, and vice versa.
concepts.key_idea: Relationship between complementation and set operations.
question_patterns: verify De Morgan's laws
show that (A intersection B)' = A' union B'
apply De Morgan's principle
prove the complement of union property
Explain the method of De Morgan's Laws.

solution_steps.explain: Find the union/intersection first, then take its complement.
Find individual complements first, then their intersection/union.
Verify that both sets contain identical elements.
